body: Negative offsets can't be used to slice a Django queryset. `queryset[-5:...]` raises `ValueError`/`AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported."), so any request with a cursor like `0:-10:0` gives a 500 instead of results. The comments say the ORM handles negative slicing, but it doesn't. And even if it did, a comment saying this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" is a red flag. Reject negative offsets (raise BadPaginationError) instead of passing them through.

This change to BasePaginator affects every paginator (Paginator, DateTimePaginator, etc.), not just the new one. With `is_prev=1`, a user-supplied negative offset (e.g. `cursor=123:-5:1`) now goes straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, and Django raises on negative indexing, so any endpoint can be made to return a 500. Before this change the offset was effectively non-negative. Keep clamping or validating the offset for all paths.

Cursor now takes negative offsets without validation, so unvalidated user input reaches every paginator. Cursor parsing should reject offset < 0 so a bad cursor gets a 400 rather than a crash deeper in the stack.

`get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`, but the audit log endpoint uses `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime` and this raises TypeError when the next/prev cursor is built. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer, which then gets compared against a timestamp column in `build_queryset` (`datetime <= 1690000000000`), which fails or matches the wrong rows. This paginator only works for numeric keys. For the audit log it needs DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversion, e.g. by subclassing DateTimePaginator.

When the offset is negative, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares against a smaller number than the page size, so the extra-row trimming logic breaks. This is another sign that the negative-offset path was never exercised.

`organization_context.member` is Optional; it is None when the user isn't a member of the org, e.g. staff or a non-superuser who gets through the permission checks another way. `organization_context.member.has_global_access` then raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Guard it with `organization_context.member is not None and ...`. Also, `request.user.is_superuser` checks the raw flag rather than an active superuser session (`is_active_superuser(request)`), which bypasses Sentry's superuser session and sudo model. Gating a code path on this is inconsistent with the rest of the API.

Pagination is a per-request choice made from `optimized_pagination`, but the cursors each paginator produces aren't compatible. DateTimePaginator encodes millisecond timestamps, while OptimizedCursorPaginator treats `cursor.value` as a raw number compared directly against `datetime`. If a client follows a Link header with the flag toggled, or gets a cursor from one path and uses it on the other, it gets wrong results or errors. Also, nothing here performs better than DateTimePaginator: the query is the same, with extra unsafe branches. Consider dropping this path entirely.
Minor: trailing whitespace here and on line 72. Lint/pre-commit will flag it.
